what.text: An activity diagram shows a flow: the steps of a business process or a use case, in order, with their conditions.

token.text: Picture a token moving through it. It starts at the initial node: a solid black dot.

action.text: Each action is a rounded rectangle, named with a verb. The token moves along the arrows, called edges.

decision.text: At a decision node, a diamond, the token takes exactly one path, chosen by a condition. A merge node, also a diamond, brings the alternate paths back together.

fork.text: A fork, a thick bar, splits one flow into parallel flows. A join, another bar, waits until every parallel flow arrives, then continues as one.

finals.text: Two endings. A flow final node, a circle with an X, stops only that one flow. An activity final node, a bullseye, stops every flow in the activity.

accept.text: An accept event action, a concave pentagon, waits for an event to happen.

lanes.text: Partitions, or swimlanes, show who does each action. For example: author, reviewer, and approver.

trap.text: So: decision and merge are about choice. Fork and join are about parallel work.
